name: Every recorded screen states how it differs from the screen recorded before it
notes: Verified goal-desk-iter-35 by browser-qa-agent (2026-07-31), live against the running ambient rig (backend :8301 / frontend :3301). All three acceptance states were captured this iteration: (1) the DEFAULT view (latest = screen-2026-07-31-c169546856c7, base = screen-2026-07-30-bad6387963ef) rendered the identical state -- 'rows compared 100 · rank changed 0 · side changed 0 · entered 0 · left 0' + 'The compared snapshots' ranked rows are identical.'; (2) selecting screen-2026-07-25-bd0b37ebc426 (default base resolves to screen-2026-07-20-ca185294a384) rendered the churned state -- 95/100 rank changed, 12 side changed, e.g. PEP rank 2 vs 64 (-62), UPS side support vs resistance; (3) selecting the ledger's oldest row screen-2026-06-22-3ecd45c062c7 rendered the honest 'No earlier recorded screen exists to compare against.' state. Screenshots: reports/qa/goal-desk-iter-35-evidence/J-20-identical-state.png / J-20-churned-state.png / J-20-no-earlier-state.png (all cropped from full-page captures -- a direct viewport screenshot at this scroll depth came back solid black, the same known browser-tool rendering quirk documented in goal-desk-iter-34-dev.md; full-page capture + crop is the workaround).

This script DELIBERATELY tests only the no-earlier-screen branch plus the section's structural presence, per this iteration's own NOTES/lessons ('journey-scripts/*.json must assert stable substrings, never a specific run's exact counts/dates -- J-20's own golden script must follow this from the start'). The identical/churned pair named in goal.md (2026-07-31 vs 2026-07-30, 2026-07-25 vs 2026-07-20) will stop being 'the default view' the moment a new real screen run is recorded, so pinning those ids/counts here would make the very next ambient Run Screen click a false regression -- the same trap iter-30's audit caught in J-18's script. The oldest-snapshot id (screen-2026-06-22-3ecd45c062c7) and its 'no earlier recorded screen' state are structurally permanent instead: screen snapshots are append-only (never backfilled, never re-dated), so nothing can ever be recorded with an EARLIER screen_date than this one without an explicit, never-planned backfill -- this is the same permanence argument J-12/J-13/J-14's own pinned historical ids already rest on.

Step 2 proves the Screen Comparison section renders on the DEFAULT (whatever-is-latest) view without asserting which of the three states it shows -- structurally true regardless of ledger growth, since the section always renders once any screen exists (gated on latest !== null).

Step 5 is a post-match liveness check (this era's iter-4/iter-5 lesson): a further /desk navigation AFTER the key assertions match, proving the page is still alive and rendering correctly, not merely that the match happened a moment before a crash.

expect.text: No earlier recorded screen exists to compare against.
